_comment: Register pointers whose cited LINE CONTENT differs from the revision that wrote them, each with a written `reason` saying which PR re-pins it or why nothing does. The screen FAILS on any drift not listed here and reports entries that no longer drift as STALE (non-failing, prune them). `regLines` are the register sentences the cite silences — the screen matches on cite, so one entry can cover several. Regenerate preserving reasons: node scripts/check-register-drift.mjs --update

entries.reason: Read-log, not a pointer: PP-055 lists the auto-backup line set (55, 147, 243, 256-257, 297) as ranges somebody read, and #2441 declined to re-pin it for exactly that reason — re-pinning would invent an intent the entry never stated. Listed here so the decision is on the record instead of silent drift.

History, not a live pointer: the register's PP-068 bullet reports the coordinate as it found it — `docs/README.md:71` was where the README's kept-rather-than-deleted paragraph sat then, and the sentence it named now sits at `docs/README.md:75`, whose own re-pin chain has run PP-071 -> PP-072 (rule at :4651) -> PP-073 (:4774) -> PP-065 (#2507, then :4810) -> PP-074 (#2526, shipped as #2568, then :4940) -> PP-070 (#2534, then :5013) -> PP-077 (#2578, now :5108). Re-writing PP-068's sentence would falsify the measurement it reports. #2569 (PP-075) and #2581 (PP-076) re-pin the same live cite from their own trees, so whichever docs PR merges last re-derives this entry; prune it the day the README names the rule by heading text instead of a line number.

Chronic, not accidental: the register's header bullets and entry sections quote this README sentence, and that sentence is the README's own re-pin of a pointer INTO the register — so any entry that adds register header text moves the line the pointer names, and this cite reads as drift by construction. PP-072 (#2558) minted it with the rule at :4651, PP-073 (#2567) moved it to :4774, PP-065 (#2507) to :4810, PP-074 (#2526, shipped as #2568) to :4940, PP-070 (#2534, since merged) to :5013, and PP-077 (this PR, #2578) re-pins it to :5108 — the fourteenth. The number is per-tree: #2569 (PP-075) measures :5106 and #2581 (PP-076) measures :5128 because all three edit the same header, and #2566 re-pins without minting an entry, so whichever merges last re-derives this one. Prune it the day the README points at the rule by heading text instead of a line number.
